newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk magazine editor sentenced for Erbakan cartoon.
newsitem.headline: Turk magazine editor sentenced for Erbakan cartoon.

text.p: A Turkish court on Wednesday imposed a prison sentence and fine on the editor of a humour magazine for publishing a cartoon which it said insulted Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, Anatolian news agency said.
Kutlu Esendemir, of Leman magazine, was given a three-and-a-half month jail sentence and fined 2,300,000 Turkish lira ($17), Anatolian said.
The agency said the caricature, published last June, showed Erbakan, in his underwear, being bathed by his coalition partner and foreign minister Tansu Ciller.
The court found the accompanying caption was an infringement of Erbakan's personal rights.
Leman, a mass-selling leftist humour magazine, has a reputation for satirical portraits of politicians.
Erbakan came to office last June when his Islam-based Welfare Party formed a coalition government with Ciller's conservative True Parth Party.
